notes: Company background: mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics). Embeds assistant into product UI and customer support flow.
Primary constraint: keep inference unit economics predictable for self-serve customers while not increasing latency.
They prefer starting on Hosted API for fast iteration then move to Dedicated when predictable throughput emerges.
Quote from CTO: 'We want predictable token economics and a clear migration path to dedicated infra with minimal code changes.'
POC specifics: 3 endpoints instrumented (chat, embed, rerank). Typical session length ~150 tokens, peak concurrent sessions ~1k during batch sync runs.
Cost-sensitivity: internal target is <$0.0006 per token equivalent for production traffic; current POC at ~$0.0014/token on Hosted defaults.
Latency/throughput targets: p50 < 120ms chat, sustained 800-1,200 TPS for embeddings refresh windows, reranking jobs batched offline OK up to 5s.
Security: require SSO (SAML), audit logs forwarded to Splunk, customer-managed KMS for key separation in Dedicated mode.
Technical asks: examples of batching configuration, KV/prefix cache behavior, recommended quantization profile for Llama-2-13B family, fallbacks for capacity events.
POC findings: enabling 16-token batching with dynamic padding reduced token compute ~18% but increased p95 by ~30ms; caching warm paths showed 40% token reduction for repeated queries.
Requested deliverables: 1) cost-optimization workshop agenda + runbook, 2) Dedicated pricing options (monthly commit vs burst), 3) migration checklist and sample configs.
Procurement note: wants line-item ARR projection (year 1) tied to batching/caching assumptions.
SE recommendation (Priya): run a 90m workshop with sample profiles: baseline, conservative quant, aggressive quant + caching, and projected unit economics for each.
Customer is evaluating competitors but values Redwood's migration story and rollout tools (canary + rollback, prefix cache).
use_case_summary: Primary: in-product conversational assistant to reduce CS load and improve UX retention.
Secondary: nightly embeddings refresh for search + reranking for top-N suggestions during product journeys.
Workload mix: 65% chat (low latency), 25% embeddings (bulk throughput during windows), 10% reranking (batchable).
